# Does sharing one controller across three motion inputs make their capabilities equivalent?

> **Current answer:** M3imic can share one policy across robot-joint, SMPL-X, and five-end-effector references, but sparse end-effector commands trade full-body fidelity for robustness; each modality requires separate accuracy, success, and hardware-failure acceptance.

## Credibility and review status

- **Handbook level:** `L3 Reviewed engineering conclusion`
- **Level note:** This conclusion has passed the Handbook EngineeringClaim review gate.
- **Confidence:** `0.76`
- **Confidence rationale:** Training and unseen-motion tables plus official code support a shared controller and a modality trade-off; hardware reliability statistics remain incomplete.
- **Safety level:** `caution`

- Paired robot, SMPL-X, and end-effector references are temporally aligned.
- Deployment uses the reported G1 observation and action contracts.

## Result

- M3imic can share one policy across robot-joint, SMPL-X, and five-end-effector references, but sparse end-effector commands trade full-body fidelity for robustness; each modality requires separate accuracy, success, and hardware-failure acceptance.

## Limitations

- Paired robot, SMPL-X, and end-effector references are temporally aligned.
- Deployment uses the reported G1 observation and action contracts.
